The feed is CockpitSnapshotProvider, which already runs in the game once per renderFrame and is already proved unwritable-through (AC-SNAPSHOT, 106 write attempts landed nothing). No panel may reach past it. ⚠ FOUND BY REVIEW — INFO CURRENTLY DESCRIBES THE WRONG BODY, and retiring BodyInfo is what makes it visible. BodyInfo describes the SELECTED body (selectTarget, main.js:6570-6611, never touches focusIndex) while the INFO panel's snapshot block is built from focusIndex (CockpitSnapshot.js:87-124). Both are on screen today, so the divergence is invisible; with BodyInfo suppressed in HELM, selecting a body would leave INFO describing something else and read as 'INFO is broken'. RESOLVED FROM MAX'S OWN CHARTER WORDS rather than by asking again — he specified INFO as 'info about whichever system object is SELECTED', so INFO follows SELECTION and the focusIndex wiring is the defect. ⭐ AND THE CASUALTY HUNT PAID: BodyInfo's RADIUS line and its Rings / Clouds / Atmosphere chips have no INFO row and no snapshot field at all. acceptanceCriteria.statement: The screensaver still loops. AutopilotNavSequence (671 lines) is act TWO — autoNav.onTourComplete fires it and it performs the nav computer, with weighted styles, a faked blinking cursor and real drills, to pick the next star. It does that by calling openNavComputer/closeNavComputer, which in HELM must now drive the COCKPIT's NAV panel rather than opening a DOM overlay on top of the cockpit. If this breaks, the game's default idle state dead-ends after one tour. ⚠ TWO REVIEW FINDINGS. (1) setPlayerPosition IS DESTRUCTIVE, NOT A SYNC — NavComputer.js:912-930 empties _localStars, calls _resetPrismLoad(), nulls _selectedNavStar and rewrites the whole local frame. Wiring it to the four focus sites (focusShip/Planet/Star/Moon) means pressing Tab while drilled into PRISM wipes the star list and the selection; worse, if a focus change lands inside AutopilotNavSequence's 20x300ms _localStars retry (AutopilotNavSequence.js:375-388) the list is emptied under it, no pick happens, and _finish() runs with no _pendingAction — a silent dead-end of the screensaver loop. So the state appliers SPLIT IN TWO: an ARRIVAL applier (setPlayerPosition + openToCurrentSystem + _currentSystemName + setExternalTarget) fired once per system, and a FOCUS applier (setCurrentBody only) fired from the four focus sites. (2) The ORRERY autopilot button leaves the DOM overlay OPEN over the cockpit: setOnAutopilotToggle routes to the hands-off start, which flips the regime, but nothing closes #nav-computer-overlay — so the cockpit renders underneath a full-screen overlay whose _navRenderLoop is still driving the OTHER instance, and the sequence then performs on a panel nobody can see. The HELM-entry applier must close the DOM overlay on the ORRERY->HELM transition.

acceptanceCriteria.statusNote: ⭐ 2026-07-31 — THE PREMISE DISSOLVED WHEN INCREMENT 7 SHIPPED; this AC has no game-side surface to settle against. THE GAME NEVER LETTERBOXES THE COCKPIT: main.js:2709-2710 hands the picker {x:0, y:0, width: innerWidth, height: innerHeight} with the comment "The cockpit target is full-screen"; RetroRenderer.js:808-814/844 sizes cockpitTarget to the window with no aspect lock; the cockpit pass (RetroRenderer.js:956-964) never calls setViewport at all — CockpitRig.test.js:298 is a committed regression guard that forbids it; main.js:10174 tracks window aspect. So x=y=0 always in HELM and the two conventions cannot disagree. The divergence is REAL, MEASURED AND LIVE-OBSERVED, but only in the lab harness (cockpit-screens-lab.html:799-804 feeds one `y` to renderer.setViewport, whose y is bottom-up, while PanelPicker.js:95-100 reads it top-down; they part when the letterbox slack H-h is odd). Evidence exists after all: cockpit-zoom-to-panel-2026-07-29/evidence/live-pass-1-gaps.json:285 records yConventionsAgree false at 1922x1082 and true at 1102x1002. The 25.4%-of-14,408 FIGURE is not recoverable from source — a reviewer recomputed the rate from the committed eyeViewport() and got 28.9-39.8% depending on the sweep set, so the percentage was a property of a size list nobody kept. RECOMMENDED DISPOSITION: moot against this build; nothing is painted wrong and no click can land wrong. ⚠ LATENT FRAGILITY WORTH KEEPING: the cockpit picker is the ONLY hit-test in main.js that assumes canvas origin = window origin — its siblings correct for it (main.js:4575, :4710 subtract rect.left). If the canvas ever stops filling the window, the cockpit picker silently acquires exactly this defect.

realStarCatalog / realFeatureCatalog (main.js:263, :270, :2848-2849) — the precondition for the far-companion chip and the component sub-view.

The lab's inline assembly in cockpit-screens-lab.html (GLTFLoader :637/:684, scene :469, lights :495/:498, mover :838, picker :849) — the code this increment extracts.
outputs: A shared cockpit rig module both the lab and the game construct (AC-ONE-RIG-TWO-HOSTS).
A cockpit render pass in the game's frame, HELM-gated.
The cockpit NavComputer instance — a SECOND NavComputer alongside the DOM one main.js builds at :2847. Both exist; which one is live follows the regime.

The warp sequence, save/load, and the mobile dock / speed-dial controls.
The full suite: 2275 passed / 4 skipped + the 15 known vendor collection errors.

NavComputer's own behaviour — this increment installs callbacks and a host; it does not change the class. The escape rework's threat model (src/ui/__tests__/NavComputer.escape.test.js header) stands: a new ESC evasion gets a line in the DECLINED list, not a wider pattern.

designDecisions.decision: The DOM overlay retirement happens in increment 7, together with first light, rather than as a following increment.
designDecisions.why: Max chose it when asked. DIEGETIC-ONLY is his founding ruling and he did not want a period of double HUD.
designDecisions.recommendationWas: SPLIT — first light in increment 7 (cockpit renders, panels live, NAV interactive, overlays still present), retirement in increment 8. The stated risk: first light and demolition in one increment opens a second front across SupercruiseHud, BodyInfo, the NavComputer overlay and the 320² target circle while nothing has ever rendered in-game, it removes the overlay you would otherwise compare a wrong panel against, and it forces the ORRERY answer immediately. Max was told this and confirmed. Recorded so the trade-off is legible if the increment turns out large, not as a hedge.

designDecisions.decision: ORRERY keeps the nav computer and BodyInfo; SupercruiseHud, the 320² target circle and the debug physics rows retire in both modes.
designDecisions.why: The program's own ruling required the contract to give ORRERY-with-zero-HUD an answer rather than break it silently. Investigated before asking: the N key that opens the nav computer is NOT mode-gated (main.js:9695), so retiring it globally would leave ORRERY unable to pick a destination by hand — functional, not cosmetic. SupercruiseHud is already gated on `_scManual || scPilot.isActive`, so retiring it costs ORRERY nothing. The discriminator Max chose is OPERABLE vs READOUT: the readouts are HELM concepts and belong on the glass; the two machines you operate need a home in a mode with no cockpit.
designDecisions.notThe: This is NOT the 'split by mode' option rejected at program open. That option was the whole HUD coexisting with the cockpit. This is which mode hosts two operable surfaces, and it was put to Max as exactly that.

designDecisions.decision: The lab's inline cockpit assembly is extracted into a module both hosts construct, and the lab is converted to a caller. Taken without asking Max — it is an engineering call, not a product one.
designDecisions.why: The alternative is two copies of the GLB load, lights, eye camera and panel rig. This program has been bitten five times by two instruments that disagreed, and 'the lab passes where the generator fails' is already its named worst case. A second copy would also mean every future cockpit change gets made twice or silently once.
designDecisions.cost: This is the increment's hidden bulk and it was not in the handoff's four-item list. src/main.js contains only CockpitSnapshotProvider; PanelHost, PanelMover, PanelPicker, NavSource and NavPanel appear in it zero times.

designDecisions.decision: Head decoupling is its own step immediately after this increment. Glass carries as-is, with no screen-space refraction.
designDecisions.why: Decoupling is a feel knob wanting lab sliders and Max's eye; bundled, neither first light nor the decoupling can be judged cleanly, and a wrong time constant reads as 'the cockpit is broken'. Refraction was never built at all — increment 3's canopy is a plain mesh with a visibility toggle — and sampling the composited world is separate work that does not block flying. The cockpit still renders as its own pass, for the precision and resolution reasons, not only the refraction one.

designDecisions.decision: The cockpit's tone regime is part of the rig's contract, not the host's: an explicit ACES curve at exposure 1.25 is applied to the cockpit sample inside RetroRenderer's composite, and the two numbers are exported from the rig so the lab reads them too.
designDecisions.why: VERIFIED IN node_modules/three/build/three.module.js: three r0.183 hard-forces `toneMapping = NoToneMapping` unless `currentRenderTarget === null || isXRRenderTarget`. The lab renders the cockpit STRAIGHT TO CANVAS with ACESFilmicToneMapping + exposure 1.25 (cockpit-screens-lab.html:466-467); the game renders it INTO a target, so it would silently get no tone mapping at all. One rig, two materially different cockpits, with nothing to say so — exactly the drift AC-ONE-RIG-TWO-HOSTS exists to prevent, arriving through a path no boundary review would catch. main.js:3831-3833 already records this three behaviour.
designDecisions.whyNotOtherwise: The alternative was deleting the lab's ACES so both hosts are NoToneMapping and re-tuning DEFAULT_COCKPIT_LIGHTS under Max's eye. Rejected because it throws away lighting he has already judged and costs him a tuning session; this way the look he approved is what ships. If it reads wrong at first light, re-tuning is still available.

designDecisions.decision: EYE_FOV (70), EYE_NEAR (0.005) and EYE_FAR are exported from the rig as the single source; both hosts construct their camera from them, and the game's FOV setting also writes the cockpit camera.
designDecisions.why: The lab pins fov 70 with a comment citing Settings.js:40 as 'the FOV the framing is judged at' (cockpit-screens-lab.html:305, :474) while the game side specified nothing — three's default is 50, which would show a cockpit subtending ~40% more of the view than Max approved, AND PanelMover re-solves fill from the live fov every solve (PanelMover.js:294-310) so the zoomed panel would land at a size he never judged. Following the slider (index.html:190 gives him a live fov control) is required for coherence: if the world's fov changes and the cockpit's does not, the canopy stops framing the view it is supposed to frame.

designDecisions.decision: The HUD slot is gated INSIDE _applyHudVisibility() (main.js:377-391) with _scManual added to its decision, and all fourteen direct retroRenderer.setHud(...) callers are converted to call it. setScManual then calls _applyHudVisibility().
designDecisions.why: Gating at setScManual alone does not work and review proved it with a sequence: boot HELM (suppressed) -> warp -> spawnSystem:4756-4767 unconditionally restores the HUD on arrival -> the minimap is back on top of the cockpit with no further regime flip to re-suppress it. Same for toggleGravityWell (:7132), exitGallery (:5366), the C key (:10002) and two mobile actions. AC-HELM-ONLY's own wording asks for a gate 'at the regime rather than at a visibility flag that something else can flip' — one door is the only way to honour that.

openForMax: ⛔ THE ONE OPEN QUESTION: a hard stop between build steps 7 and 8 for a first-light UAT pass, BEFORE any overlay is deleted. Review's strongest finding. The build order calls step 8 the POINT OF NO RETURN and schedules Max's UAT gate at step 11, after every deletion — so the overlays he would compare a wrong panel against are gone before he has ever looked at the cockpit. The design's own step-7 rationale says 'EVERYTHING TO HERE IS PURELY ADDITIVE: stop at this step and the game is strictly better than before, with every overlay still present to compare a wrong panel against' — and then declines to use that checkpoint. This is NOT the increment split Max declined; the increment still ships whole. It is one pause inside it, at the seam the design itself identified. AWAITING HIS ANSWER.

ORRERY's half of the 320-square minimap: this increment retires it in HELM only and leaves ORRERY exactly as it is, which matches the prior recorded ruling. If Max wants it gone in ORRERY too that is a separate decision, and it would also take the C key, the V key and gravity wells, two Settings rows, two mobile speed-dial actions and the 'now targeting' blink cue with it.

Routing the four autopilot paths into HELM has two side effects Max has not been shown: setScManual fires _updateModeSwapButton (relabels the HUD button) and _syncOrbitsToMode (turns the ORRERY orbit LINES off). Both follow from the regime genuinely changing, which is what he approved; flagged so neither is a surprise.
THE ARM — unchanged, out of scope, wants its own scoping conversation. He wants it to bend/extend with the monitor; that is generator geometry (one baked mesh, world-space vertices, no transform).
AC-NOTHING-I-HAD-GOT-LOST in cockpit-screen-content-2026-07-28 is still an open UAT gate. No agent can close it.
